register_resolvers(*, replace: bool = False) -> None

Register the resolvers to OmegaConf.

This method publishes the registered resolvers to OmegaConf. It is idempotent: calling it twice changes nothing. A resolver removed from OmegaConf (for example with OmegaConf.clear_resolvers()) is published again.

Without replace, a resolver already published by this registry, and whose key OmegaConf still knows, is not registered again. A key is skipped if OmegaConf already has a resolver for it that this registry did not publish (registered by another source), or if the registry changed since it was published. If True, the resolvers replace the resolvers that OmegaConf already has for the same keys. If False, these keys are skipped, with a warning for the ones that this registry did not publish.

False

If a key is skipped and the warnings are turned into errors. The other keys are published first.

path_resolver(path: str | PathLike[str]) -> Path

Return a resolved path object from a path or a file URL.

This resolver converts a string, or any path-like object (for example a pathlib.Path stored in the configuration), to a pathlib.Path object: it expands the user home directory (~) and resolves the path to an absolute path. A string that starts with file: (the scheme is case-insensitive) is read as a file URL: the path of the URL is used, with its percent-encoding (for example %20 for a space) decoded. In a URL, ? and # start a query and a fragment, so a file name that contains them is written %3F and %23. Any other URL with :// after a scheme of two characters or more (for example s3://bucket) is rejected: it is not a local path. Any other string is a plain path, written as is: ?, # and % are not interpreted.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default path str | PathLike[str]

The target path as a string or a path-like object, or a file: URL.

required

Returns:

Type Description Path

A fully resolved pathlib.Path object with expanded user

Path

directory and converted to absolute path.

Raises:

Type Description TypeError

If path is not a string or a path-like object.

RuntimeError

If the home directory of a ~ path cannot be determined, for example for an unknown user.

ValueError

If the path is empty (write . for the working directory); if a file: URL has no path, a host other than localhost (for example file://host/a), a query or a fragment (any ? or #, for example file:///data/run#1); or if the string is a URL with another scheme (scheme://...). A UnicodeDecodeError, a subclass of ValueError, is raised if the percent-encoding of a file: URL is not valid UTF-8.

Note

Within an OmegaConf interpolation, a path with a tilde (~) must be quoted (${hya.path:"~/data"}); unquoted, the interpolation is a grammar error.

Example 
>>> from pathlib import Path
>>> import hya
>>> from omegaconf import OmegaConf
>>> conf = OmegaConf.create({"key": "${hya.path:/my/path}"})
>>> conf.key
PosixPath('/my/path')
>>> conf = OmegaConf.create({"key": "${hya.path:file:///my/path%20to}"})
>>> conf.key
PosixPath('/my/path to')
>>> conf = OmegaConf.create({"key": '${hya.path:"~/my/path"}'})
>>> conf.key == Path("~/my/path").expanduser().resolve()
True
>>> conf = OmegaConf.create({"key": "${hya.path:${hya.path:/my/path}}"})
>>> conf.key
PosixPath('/my/path')

sha256_resolver(obj: Any) -> str

Compute the SHA-256 hash of the whole content of an object.

The configuration nodes of the object are resolved first, at any depth. A string is then hashed as is, so the result is the SHA-256 of the text, the same as other tools give. Any other value is hashed from its canonical JSON form: sorted keys, no space ([1,2], {"a":1,"b":2}, true, null) and non-ASCII characters escaped (\u00e9 for an e with an acute accent). In this form, a path or an enum is written as its string, except an enum that is also an int, a float or a str (for example an IntEnum), which is written as its value. Useful for generating consistent identifiers or cache keys from configuration values.

The hash does not keep the type of a value: the string [1] and the list [1] have the same hash, and so do an integer key and the same string key.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default obj Any

The object to compute the SHA-256 hash: a string, or a value with a JSON form (numbers, booleans, None, lists, tuples, dictionaries, ListConfig, DictConfig, paths and enums).

required

Returns:

Type Description str

The SHA-256 hash as a hexadecimal string (64 characters).

Raises:

Type Description TypeError

If a value has no JSON form (for example an array, a tensor, a data type, a set or bytes), if a key of a mapping is not a string, a number, a boolean or None, or if a mapping mixes key types that cannot be sorted.

ValueError

If a value or a key is a non-finite float (nan or inf), which has no JSON form.

MissingMandatoryValue

If a node contains a missing value (???).

Example 
>>> import hya
>>> from omegaconf import OmegaConf
>>> conf = OmegaConf.create({"key": "${hya.sha256:mystring}"})
>>> conf.key
bd3ff47540b31e62d4ca6b07794e5a886b0f655fc322730f26ecd65cc7dd5c90
>>> # Useful for generating consistent IDs
>>> conf = OmegaConf.create({"id": "${hya.sha256:experiment_v1}"})
>>> # The order of the keys does not change the hash
>>> conf = OmegaConf.create(
...     {
...         "x": {"a": 1, "b": 2},
...         "y": {"b": 2, "a": 1},
...         "hx": "${hya.sha256:${x}}",
...         "hy": "${hya.sha256:${y}}",
...     }
... )
>>> conf.hx == conf.hy
True

If the data cannot be converted to an array, for example nested lists of different lengths, or a string with a numeric dtype.

MissingMandatoryValue

If a node contains a missing value (???).

Example 
>>> import hya
>>> from omegaconf import OmegaConf
>>> conf = OmegaConf.create({"key": "${hya.np.array:[1, 2, 3]}"})
>>> conf.key
array([1, 2, 3])

>>> conf = OmegaConf.create({"a": 1, "x": ["${a}", 2], "key": "${hya.np.array:${x}}"})
>>> conf.key

Implement PyTorch resolvers for tensor creation and dtype handling.

This module provides OmegaConf resolvers that use PyTorch for tensor operations and data type specifications. The resolvers are always registered; the torch package is needed only when one of them is called, and a missing package raises an error that says how to install it. Users can create PyTorch tensors and specify dtypes directly from configuration files.

to_plain(value: Any) -> Any

Return value with its configuration nodes converted to plain, resolved objects.

OmegaConf gives a resolver the configuration node itself (ListConfig or DictConfig), and a literal such as [${x}] is a plain list that contains nodes. A resolver that reads a whole value as text or data must resolve the interpolations of these nodes, at any depth. Lists and dictionaries are searched for nodes and are returned as new containers, so value is not modified. Any other object (including a tuple) is returned as is.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default value Any

The value to convert.

required

Returns:

Type Description Any

The value without configuration nodes.

Raises:

Type Description MissingMandatoryValue

If a node contains a missing value (???).

InterpolationResolutionError

If an interpolation of a node cannot be resolved, for example a reference to a key that does not exist.

Example 
>>> from omegaconf import OmegaConf
>>> from hya.utils.config import to_plain
>>> conf = OmegaConf.create({"a": 1, "x": ["${a}", 2]})
>>> to_plain(conf.x)
[1, 2]
>>> to_plain([conf.x, {"y": conf.x}])
[[1, 2], {'y': [1, 2]}]

docs.title: hya.testing
docs.text:
Define PyTest markers for testing optional dependencies.

This module provides pytest markers that help with testing the hya library under different dependency configurations. The markers allow tests to be conditionally skipped based on whether optional packages (braceexpand, numpy, torch) are available in the test environment.

These markers are useful for ensuring tests only run when the required dependencies are present, avoiding import errors and test failures when optional packages are not installed.

For each optional package, <package>_available skips a test when the package is not installed, and <package>_not_available skips a test when it is installed: braceexpand_available, braceexpand_not_available, numpy_available, numpy_not_available, torch_available and torch_not_available.

This module imports pytest, which the testing extra installs (pip install 'hya[testing]').

Example 
>>> from hya.testing import numpy_available
>>> @numpy_available
... def test_with_numpy():
...     pass
...
